newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SUFFER SETBACK IN SARDINIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-JUVENTUS SUFFER SETBACK IN SARDINIA.

text.p: Juventus's march towards the serie A title hit a pothole on Sunday when lowly Cagliari held them 0-0 and 10-man Sampdoria came back to beat AC Milan 3-2 to stay two points adrift of the European Cup holders.

Juventus, whose Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero was sent off in the 34th minute, now have 37 points from 19 matches. They are followed by Sampdoria and Bologna, who thrashed lowly Verona 6-1, to move to 31 points.

The world club champions created few chances and were lucky to come away with a point after Montero was sent packing for a violent tackle on striker Roberto Muzzi and Cagliari came close on several occasions.
"We played nearly an hour with 10 men and never gave up," said Juve coach Marcello Lippi. "I'm satisfied with they way all my men played."
Juventus had appeared to lack a serious challenger in their title quest before Sunday, but Sampdoria's dramatic recovery in MIlan firmly established them as contenders.
"Everything's going well for us. We came back from two goals down and with 10 men -- that's not too bad at San Siro," said Sampdoria's Swedish coach, Sven Goran Eriksson.
The 1991 league champions, the surprise of the serie A season, jumped out on top in the first minute when veteran captain Roberto Mancini scored his 13th goal of the season.
The 32-year-old is now joint top scorer with Atalanta's Filippo Inzaghi and Argentine Abel Balbo, who scored two well-taken goals in Roma's 2-0 home win over Vicenza.
But things appeared to take a turn for the worst in the 22nd minute when goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron was sent off for fouling Milan's George Weah..

The 1995 World Player of the Year, in his first appearance since suffering an injury on December 22, did not hesitate in finding his old form -- equalising in the 37th minute and making it 2-1 in the 57th.

But just when victory seemed certain, Yugoslavian defender Sinisa Mihajlovic blasted home a free-kick to equalise in the 74th minute and, five minutes later, winger Marco Carparelli added the shock winner.

It was Milan's eighth defeat this season, putting them in 12th place, and the second time Sampdoria have come from behind to win at the San Siro. Mancini scored in injury time to beat Internazionale 4-3 earlier this season.
Two brilliant free-kicks by midfielder Cristiano Scapolo led Bologna's 6-1 rout of Verona, who appear likely to make an immediate return to serie B despite defeating Milan 3-1 last week.
Sweden's Kennet Andersson and Russia's Igor Shalimov also added goals as Bologna coach Renzo Ulivieri celebrated his 57th birthday.
Parma, 2-1 losers at Napoli last Sunday, bounced back as Enrico Chiesa scored in a 1-0 win over Piacenza that put them level on points with Internazioanle, held 0-0 at Perugia, and Vicenza.
Chiesa's goal was perhaps the most impressive of the day -- an acrobatic 57th minute volley from a Dino Baggio cross that left goalkeeper Massimo Taibi helpless.

Dino Zoff, who replaced Czech Zdenek Zeman as Lazio's coach on Monday, celebrated a victorious debut in his native Friuli as striker Giuseppe Signori scored twice to lead the Rome club to a 3-2 win at Udinese.
